items.text: $Y$ quasi-compact, $\mathcal L$ ample, $\mathcal M$ any invertible sheaf $\Rightarrow$ $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\otimes\mathcal M$ ample for $n\gg0$; so the ample cone spans $\operatorname{Pic}X\otimes\mathbf Q$.
Quasi-projective and projective
$f\colon X\to Y$ quasi-projective: (a) there is an invertible $\mathcal L$ on $X$ ample relative to $Y$; (b) $f$ is of finite type.
$f$ projective: (a) as before and (b$'$) $f$ is proper (finite type, separated, universally closed); separated follows from (a).

$Y$ coherent: quasi-projective $\iff$ immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\mathcal E)$, $\mathcal E$ of finite type; projective $\iff$ closed immersion (an immersion into a proper scheme is proper iff closed).
Stable under base change; proper is stable under composition (finite type, separated, universally closed).
Composition of quasi-projectives:
\mathcal L\ \text{ample on }X/Y,\ \mathcal M\ \text{ample on }Y/Z\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal L\otimes f^*\mathcal M^{\otimes n}\ \text{ample on }X/Z\ \ (n\gg0,\ Z\ \text{quasi-compact})
Proof only indicated (EGA II); the restriction « $Z$ quasi-compact » to be checked.
Proper morphisms
$f$ proper: of finite type, separated, universally closed (stable under base change and composition).
$X$ proper over $Y$, $Z$ separated over $Y$ $\Rightarrow$ every $Y$-morphism $g\colon X\to Z$ is closed.
$f$ finite type, $g\colon X\to Z$ an immersion, $Z$ proper over $Y$: $f$ proper $\iff$ $g$ a closed immersion. Closed immersions are proper.
Projective $\Rightarrow$ proper; proper does not imply projective (Chow's lemma: birationally projective).
Valuative criterion of properness
Reduce to $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. $Y$ locally noetherian, $f\colon X\to Y$:
f\ \text{proper}\iff f\ \text{of finite type and, for every trait }Y'=\operatorname{Spec}V\to Y:\quad \Gamma(X'/Y')\longrightarrow\Gamma(X'_\eta/\eta)\ \text{is bijective}
A trait: spectrum of a discrete valuation ring; two points, generic $\eta$ and closed $s$.
Injective $\iff$ separated (valuative criterion of separation). Surjective: a rational point $x\in X_\eta$; take $Y'=\overline{\{x\}}$ with reduced structure.
$Y'\to Y$ is surjective (closed image containing $\eta$), birational, separated; $Y$ normal of dimension one $\Rightarrow$ $Y'\to Y$ is an isomorphism, whose inverse is a section.
Properness of P(E)
Reduce to $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $A$ a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, $\mathcal E=\tilde M$, $M$ of finite type:
\{\text{free rank-one quotients }L\text{ of }M\}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\{\text{rank-one quotients }L_K\text{ of }M_K\},\qquad H=M\cap H_K,\ \ L=M/H
$M/H$ is of finite type, torsion-free over a principal ideal domain, hence free of rank one.
Integral and finite morphisms
$A$ a ring, $B$ an $A$-algebra, $x\in B$. Equivalent: (a) $x$ is integral over $A$:
x^n+a_1x^{n-1}+\cdots+a_n=0,\qquad a_i\in A
(b) $A[x]$ is a module of finite type over $A$; (c) $x$ lies in a subalgebra $B'\subset B$ finite over $A$.
$B$ integral over $A$ $\iff$ $B$ is the union of finite subalgebras.
Subalgebras and quotients of integral algebras are integral; the integral elements form a subalgebra, the integral closure of $A$ in $B$; transitivity: $A\to B\to C$ integral.
Integral and finite morphisms

$f$ integral (resp. finite): $f$ affine, $X=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal B$, $\mathcal B$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra integral (resp. finite, i.e. of finite type as a module) over $\mathcal O_Y$.
Stable under base change and composition ($Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal C$, $\mathcal C$ integral over $\mathcal B$, $\mathcal B$ over $\mathcal O_Y$).
